   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Kevin Cooper

In OUTLET you have sections with
text in (especially OUTLETTERS).
What kind of files are these
and, if they are text files off
a wordprocessor, how do you load
them and display them without
the main program? - Kevin Cooper

They are our own,specially comp-
ressed text files which we use
to squeeze more into OUTLET!They
cannot be displayed without an
expander routine such as we use
in OUTLET but CAN be converted
back to normal text (if your
system supports OPENTYPE files)
by altering the BASIC at around
line 1200 onwards to write to a
drive. Let me know if you want
details.                 -Brian

From Ken Stearn, FIFE

First of all, thank you for your
prompt and detailed reply to my
query which you printed in
OUTLETTERS Vol.43. It makes
everything all so much clearer.

May I trouble you further by
asking if you could send me the
BASIC you mentioned? I have
attempted something along the
same lines but would like to see
how a 'master' does it!!

One other thing, is it possible
to alter HARD 24, Vol.34 to
print across a full-sized page.
This is an excellent program
which gives good shaded dumps
from a 24-pin printer.
                   - Ken Stearn

To Ken Stearn from Brian Cavers

You should, by now,have received
a copy of a simple BASIC DUMP
routine but I'll include it in
this issue as "BASDUMP" too as
others may be interested in just
how graphics are sent a printer.

I have added more REM comments
to the version in this issue to
make it as clear as possible. It
is slow but, being BASIC, it can
be examined and understood much
more easily, as well as modified
to get special effects. Once the
principle is grasped you could
store the data from a small
image (part of the screen) in a
string and send it quickly,e.g.,
a copyright sign.

Regarding HARD 24, as mentioned
in that program, both Ron and I
only have 8-pin printers (aaah!)
so I can't help you directly but
I'm sure the author of HARD 24,
Carlo Vireca, will be glad to
help.His address is on the front
page of the program.

                        - Brian

Mr. Dave Burk, 17 Barnard Close,
Duston, Northampton, NN5 6LB

Dear Chezron,

Once again may I join the other
subscribers in heaping praise
upon you for the very efficient
way you run Outlet. As always
the quality of the articles
etc., is very high although as a
humble non-disc drive user I
feel we are in danger of losing
out due to the amount of systems
you are catering for.

On a more constructive note, may
I suggest two ideas for possible
compilations, namely, one for
the series you did on program
protection and perhaps one for a
collection of clipart.

Now for a HELP request. Can
anyone help me with a copy of
the code (TS2CODE) in Tasign as
mine has become corrupted.

That's all for now, keep up the
good work,
                    - Dave Burk

To Dave Burk from Brian Cavers

Thanks, Dave. I've put your full
address so you can be contacted
direct.

Your ideas for compilations have
been noted and, in fact, the one
for clip art has coincided with
the launch of our first clip art
compilation from OUTLET called
OUTLET EXTRA 2(CLIPPER 1).At the
time of writing the price is
undecided but I expect it to be
the same as a single issue of
OUTLET. However, regrettably,
CLIPPER 1 is only available on
Disciple/+D, +3 and SAM format
so what you say about tape users
losing out to the mighty drive
has some truth in it. Sorry.
                        - Brian

From Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS


Can anyone please advise ?. How
can I reduce the level of
interference put out by the +D
and/or the Spectrum so that I
can use them with a morse decode
software program fed from the
loudspeaker output of my short-
wave receiver. When the +D
'turns', the noise it generates
just blots out my short wave
radio. Even my tv adds noise.

    Help please someone !!!

Brian Gaff to Malcolm Goodman


This is a common problem and I
am afraid there is no one answer
to it. You could for instance
coat the inside of all casings
with conductive paint, then
earth it, and screen the cables.
However, as long as you have a
direct connection to the
receiver, the mush will get in!

Most Hams use terminal units
which can have an opto-isolator
in them. This breaks the direct
connection, and, with good
screening and an aerial as far
away from the computer/TV as
possible, the problem is much
reduced.

For more info, I feel sure the
RSGB could point you toward a
Ham computing club who may have
already solved your particular
problem.

I have myself experienced the
interference you mention, and
the only thing I found that
helped a bit was to wind the
lead that carries the signal to
the Spectrum, around a ferrite
torroid a few times. This seemed
to be best done at the Spectrum
end. I hope that helps.

                   - Brian Gaff

From Chris Oliver, STAFFS.

Dear Brian & Ron,

Re. Paul Preston's enquiry in
OUTLET 44 about the Opus
Discovery "File Manipulation
Table". This is TABLE #14 which
tabulates the start addresses
for DOS routines as follows:-

 199F.TABLE_14...DEFB 0

 19A0...DEFW 19A2

 19A2...DEFW 0D18 ; MAKE_CAT
opens the CAT channel. On entry
DE points to the start of the
parameter block, BC holds the
length of the block and A holds
the 'channel_open' flags.

 19A4...DEFW 0BB0 ; PUT_BLK
writes a block to disc.

 19A6...DEFW 0D81 ; FIND_FL find
a file having the same name as
that stored at (IX+8). On exit
the 'record_No' is in BC.

 19A8...DEFW 0DE8 ; MAKE_FL make
a file in the CAT.

 19AA...DEFW 0DA8 ; GET_FRE find
the largest gap on the disc. On
exit BC holds the length of the
gap and DE holds the record No.
of the file preceding the gap.
Note that if two gaps of the
same length are found, the first
is ignored.

 19AC...DEFW 0E8C ; POSN_BC find
the record No. held in BC from
the CAT file.

 19AE...DEFW 0E83 ; READ_CAT
reads a byte from the CAT file
into the A reg. On exit HL holds
the address of the byte in the
buffer.

 19B0...DEFW 0ABB ; WRITE_CAT
writes a byte from the A reg to
disc.

The above is how the table
appears in version 2.1 DOS. In
version 2.2, things are shuffled
about a bit, and TABLE 14 sits
at 1812H and will look like
this, to find similar routines
at relevant addresses:-

 1812 DEFB 0
 1813 DEFW 1815
 1815 DEFW 0DD4 ; MAKE_CAT
 1817 DEFW 0C63 ; PUT_BLK
 1819 DEFW 0E3D ; FIND_FL
 181B DEFW 0EA4 ; MAKE_FL
 181D DEFW 0E64 ; GET_FRE
 181F DEFW 0F48 ; POSN_BC
 1821 DEFW 0F3F ; READ_CAT
 1823 DEFW 0B6E ; WRITE_CAT

What a genius! I hear you cry,
to disassemble the Discovery ROM
just like that. But as the
applause fades away, I must
confess that I extracted the
info from a disassembly produced
by Marcel van Dongen, which I
obtained from him in 1989. His
address then was, and probably
still is:-

       Fred Ruyschstr.65,
        2563 VW Den Haag,
            Holland.

        Tel: 070/600153.


   ...and he charged 18 Guilders
(approx `6) for it. Although
Marcel writes excellent English,
deciphering the book is tedious
as it has been photocopied with
rather poor definition. So 4s
can be mistaken for As, Bs for
8s, Ds for 0s, Es for Fs etc.,
but it does exist and the 108
pages are crammed full of useful
information. The main section is
a full disassembly of the 2.1
DOS, then follow 4 appendices:-

 A: Routines in 2.2 and 2.22.

 B: Memory map.

 C: Data sheet for the W01770,
plus some tables that are
virtually unreadable in my copy,
plus a flag summary.

 D: Organisation of the disc,
sectors,tracks, blocks, records.

And last of all, a good index to
the routines, giving addresses
for both 2.1 and 2.2 versions.

Hope this helps.   Chris Oliver.


Many thanks, Chris.
                    - Brian

From:Haydn McWatters,NTH IRELAND

Dear Sirs,

Thank you for your prompt reply
and my first copy of OUTLET
(043).I found it very interest-
ing and learnt a lot from your
readers' letters.

I've just bought a +D interface
and disc drive from DATEL and I
am very pleased with it. It is
more reliable than the micro-
drives I had. In your answer to
one of your readers you said
that the +D and Interface 1 were
not compatible. As I intended to
use the Interface 1 serial port
to drive a Brother 4 (HR5)
printer I've a few questions.
Perhaps you could help.

1) The +D interface has a Centr-
onics printer port; the Brother
HR5 a RS232c serial port.Accord-
ing to the manual the HR5 was
made with either a serial RS232c
port or Centronics port.

On examining the PCB there is
provision for a Centronics port.
Is it possible to modify it?

2) if this is not possible I
have the opportunity to buy a
second hand Plus 2 Spectrum
(grey). Is the printer port the
same as Interface 1?

3) In one of your letters was a
mention of programs "PICK IT
POKE IT" and "PLUS D HACKER".Are
these programs still available?

4) I also have a PRISM VTX  5000
MODEM.Are there any compatabil-
ity problems with the Plus D?

        THANKING YOU BOTH

        HAYDN MC WATTERS

Brian Gaff to Haydn McWatters

There is no way I know of to
operate a +D and Interface 1 at
the same time. Both have a ROM
which pages in when there is a
syntax error in normal Spectrum
Basic so they just fight each
other for control!

The Brother HR5 does come in two
variants, as you say, but as to
whether it is possible to actua-
lly add the other to an existing
printer, I very much doubt it!

The VTX 5000 works with a +D but
I doubt if the disc interface
will be reliable when mounted on
the ribbon cable.The cable skews
the very high frequency pulses
and that confuses the +D!

The grey +2 RS232 has a serial
port which uses a plug very
similar to the BT telephone
ones. They are available from
Tandy etc. Note that the RS232
software in ROM is very crude
compared to Interface 1,you need
2 pokes to create a "b" channel!

The only problem is I know of no
+2 that has ever successfully
driven both a +D and a VTX5000
simultaneously. The reason is
that the extra chips in the 128K
machine lessen the peripheral
driving power quite a lot.

The VTX 5000 also needs a short
MC routine to boot in the ROM on
a +2, though if you use software
loaded from disc, this is not a
problem.

There can also be a clash of
roms if OPENTYPE files are in
use when a VTX ROM routine is
called.

If you use a 48K machine, you
could connect the VTX and +D via
a Currah Uslot, though the disc
interface would stick up in the
air.

Pick-Poke-it seems a victim of
the demise of MGT. +D Hacker is
still around; contact Steve's
Software on 0223 235150 between
6pm and 9pm for current details.

Sorry I cannot be more helpful,
I would advise you to get a
cheap Centronics printer, as the
HR5 is a bit limited.

By the way, don't be tempted to
get a black +2A, they are not
compatible with the +D in 128K
mode, and need a Fixit to even
work in 48K!

                         - B.G.

ALAN RUTHERFORD,33 MONTGOMERY RD
COVE,FARNBOROUGH,HANTS,GU14 0AY

Thank you for an excellent maga-
zine even though it seems to be
getting slanted towards SAM.I am
still using my trusty 48K Model
3 which has served me very well
and suits all uses I'm likely to
need. The only advantage I can
see of SAM is greater colour for
artwork plus some more memory.

I've two 16k Ram packs from the
old ZX81. Do you know if anybody
has succeeded in linking it to a
48K Spectrum? It should be poss-
ible to page the extra memory in
to make the Spectrum a true 48K
memory machine. If you know of
anyone could you let me know or
publish my address in the mag.?

Brian Cavers to Alan Rutherford

Years ago there used to be a 16K
to 48K Spectrum memory upgrade
with an optional extra 32K to
boost the Spectrum up to 80K.The
extra 32K was paged in somehow.
My guess is that an electronics
enthusiasts could probably find
some way to link your extra RAM.
Any ideas anyone?

                        - Brian

From: John Redfern, LONDON

I thought I would write to you,
firstly to have my say on a
couple of points and secondly to
offer a couple of tips.

The availability of certain
Computer magazines in my local
branch of W.H. Smith is getting
less and less. Most are only
available on order.Its obviously
up to the manager of each shop
as to which magazines he puts on
his shelves. How many people
know that the late-lamented ZX
Computing was not even available
on order from WHS for the last
few months of its life as it had
been removed from the WHS order
lists.

As any publisher or journalist
will tell you, unless a magazine
is stocked by WHS it is most
unlikely to survive!!!

I recently purchased the new
BetaDOS for my Plus D and set it
up in accordance with the
manual. All seemed to be O.K.
until I started getting lots of
Sector Errors on my 3.5" drive
(the 5.25" seemed O.K.).

After a frustrating couple of
weeks blaming a new box of discs
and BetaDOS itself and still
having the problem with a
further new box of discs, I de-
cided that it must be the Drive
itself.

When carefully dismantling the
drive, inspection revealed a
build up of dust and fluff
around the drive heads similar
to that which you get on the
stylus of your record player.
This I removed with an artist's
brush and fine tweezers.A gener-
al clean up of the rest of the
mechanism with the brush and a
good blow out followed by
careful lubrication of the head
moving mechanism with a little
WD40 on a cocktail stick seems
to have effected a considerable
improvement on its reliability,
with (so far) no more of the
dreaded 'Sector Errors'.

If you decide to clean your own
drive you'll find you normally
only have to remove the covers.

DON'T touch any of the parts of
the drive itself with your
screwdriver or you will upset
the very delicate settings and
only use a soft artist's brush
in the vicinity of the heads.

It should be pointed out that
BetaDos works best with an
UNMODIFIED System File, having
things like Pick-Poke-It for
instance on your system causes
some unexplained problems.

My +2 doesn't like Tasword +2.
When in use for a short while
the text file starts corrupting,
mainly with characters from the
second character set.This slowly
gets worse until eventually the
whole lot locks up and I have to
power down and reload.

If I manage to get an uncorrupt-
ed text file, as soon as I print
it out, it completely corrupts
and has to be reset. The +2 has
been away to be repaired twice
but they don't seem to be able
to cure the problem. The program
works O.K. on my 128.

Does anyone have any idea what
is causing the problem?

         Yours sincerely

          John Redfern

Brian Cavers to John Redfern

Thanks, John.

What interfaces have you got in
the back of the +2 -just the +D?
It's worth giving the edge conn-
ector a good clean with a rubber
eraser to remove any build up of
oxidation.


Are the interface and Spectrum
solidly linked or is there a
little"give"? It may help if you
can secure it in some way - even
tape it to your desk!We Spectrum
users have done all sorts over
the years to keep the engines
turning.

On Page 25 of these OUTLETTERS
Brian Gaff says the black +2A is
not compatible with the +D in
128K mode so I assume you must
have a grey model? How did you
get Tasword +2 on disc anyway?
If converted with Tascon +2 did
you make an error in the process
e.g. code length? (I've not seen
the program -it may be automatic
for all I know).Convert it again
if not sure.

Anyone else have any ideas?

                        - Brian.

From Norman Haigh, W. YORKS


I hadn't really considered a
printer. However, being a sub-
scriber to OUTLET and SDC, I
have now reconsidered. Both disc
magazines have the option to
print out pages allowing one to
read instructions and tutorials
at leisure without having to
load the disc into the computer.

I am considering purchase of a
Citizen Swift 24 but I have not
been able to read any reviews on
this model. The local computer
store sells only the 120D. I am
unable to attend any of the
fairs. Do you have the address
of a Citizen distributor please?

Can you recommend an interface
for the Spectrum? Datel have two
and Romantic Robot have one. Is
a through-port required for use
with a Disciple Interface?

        Yours sincerely,

          Norman Haigh

Brian Cavers to Norman Haigh

I've not used a Citizen Swift 24
printer myself but here's some
info...

24-pin, Centronics, 8K buffer,
good paper handling- push/pull
tractor fed thru' back & bottom,
auto-load,paper parking, handles
envelopes, single sheets. No dip
switches - adjustments made to
front panel.6 fonts.Draft speed:
100cps, Best:42cps. RRP:`389+VAT
(colour pack can be added later
for about `38+VAT). I was very
impressed with what I read about
this machine. It looks good
value. I wouldn't mind getting
one myself if I could afford it!
Now, where to get one...

Well my foregoing info goes back
over the last 6 months or so and
the price may vary.For instance,
SILICA SYSTEMS latest offer is:
RRP `428.88, Starter kit:`29.95,
Colour Kit:`44.65, total:`503.48
THEIR PRICE:`304.33,inc.VAT+post
the lot!

The "starter kit" is two discs
with printer software for IBM,ST
Amiga, etc.,so may not interest
you other than to use as blank
discs; printer cable (wrong sort
for you - see later); 200 sheets
continuous paper,ditto labels; 5
envelopes. SILICA are at 1-4 the
Mews, Hatherley Rd., Sidcup,Kent
DA14 4DX (Tel:081 309 1111).

However...

NATIONWIDE COMPUTERS,19 Progress
Way, Croydon, Surrey CR0 4XD
(Tel: 081 681 6952) offer the
SWIFT24 at `212+VAT and delivery
or the SWIFT24X(this is the wide
carriage version) at `299 +VAT +
delivery. Ring them to find the
delivery cost.

You could also ring Citizen on
0895 72621 who may be able to
suggest another source.

The cable you need is a BBC-type
(STATE +D) `7.99+`1 postage from
PBT ELECTRONICS LTD.,Port Talbot
Workshops, Unit 17,Addison Road,
Port Talbot, SA12 6HZ (Tel:0639
885008).

Let me know how you get on.

I'm not quite sure what you mean
by "an interface for a Spectrum"
as your +D or Disciple has both
printer port and back-up device.
Once you've got the printer and
cable you just plug in and go!
(That's the theory - most of us
spend the afternoon figuring out
what goes where!)

If you do get the printer, why
not send us a detailed review as
others (including me) would be
interested?
                       - Brian

From Vincent L. Jacks,LONDON SE9

Dear Sirs,

I write to ask you if you could
kindly help me with a few prob-
lems that I have at this time.
Firstly, before I go on I should
state I know absolutely nothing
re:machine code programming and
only write in BASIC when I write
my own programs.

            PROBLEMS
1. I have just sent off for the
PLUS D disc drive and interface
from DATEL ELECTRONICS. I own
Tasword Plus Two and, although I
think it to be a great package
(wp) I would like to transfer it
to disk(both program and files).

I wrote to Tasman and they say
that because it's in machine
code it cannot be done. Do you
know better and can you help?

2.I also own OCP ART STUDIO.Like
the above, can it be transferred
to disk also? Can you help?

3.I've Gilsoft's PAWS. Again,I'd
like it on disk. (Again), can it
be done and how?

4.Re:Tasword Plus Two again. You
know the awful character set you
can't read and if you change
window size you get that horrid
Spectrum ROM character set? (You
have guessed it)Can a new char-
acter set be installed to use
with the 64 character text. How
please?

5. This one's not really a prob-
lem but,re:ALL the above, do you
have any utilities I could buy
to help solve all my problems?

Any help that you could forward
would be most appreciated. I'm
looking forward to owning a disc
drive. Tape has made me grey-
haired over the years but, I
wonder,if these utilities cannot
be transferred, will my hair now
fall out?

Thanks for a wonderful issue of
OUTLET(my first)and I am looking
forward to all the rest on 3.5"
disk.
      Most sincerely yours,

        Vincent L. Jacks

Brian Cavers to Vincent Jacks

Thanks, Vincent.

1.I believe Datel include a copy
of FORMAT magazine (INDUG user
group).If you join the group you
can order TASCON +2. It converts
Tasword +2 to disc (`3.95).

2 and 3. You should be able to
put Art Studio and PAWS on disc
by using the magic button(see +D
manual)but both use code to load
and save files and are difficult
to alter. Derek Morgan had an ad
in OUTBOARD for the ART STUDIO
conversion. His address is there
in a new ad so ask him if he has
it still (the old ad may just
have got pushed out of OUTBOARD
by new stuff).

4. Yes, we have three character
sets that will work with Tasword
+2 (as well as Tas 2 and 3). In
OUTLET 14 is MINICHARS 2 and 3
(2 is square-ish, 3 is rounder)
and in OUTLET 17 is MINICHAR 4
which is similar to 2. All you
do is load the Tas code then
LOAD "MINICHAR" CODE 54528 and
reSAVE the TAS code.

I used to have a wonderful head
of hair but this has decreased
in proportion to the increase in
the speed of the drives used...
Microdrive, Opus, +3, Disciple,
SAM... Be VERY careful.
                     - Brian

From Peter R. Morgalla, HERTS.




Dear Ron & Brian,

Regarding your reply to George
Till about printing on A4 paper,
The correct page length is 70
lines, assuming the printer is
set to 1/6 inch line feed. My
TW2 (SAM) program is set up with
graphic CHR$ 143, graph/cap/8,
as code 27,67,70.

Incidentally, I occasionally use
2/3 A4 tractor feed paper which
needs the page length set to 48
lines.

I think TABLOID is super. One
minor point though, I occasion-
ally find that certain lines are
displaced to the left - see
attached printout. Is this
something that can be fixed? I
also print out a directory of
the disk to use as list of
contents and with the printer
set to condensed mode and 24/216
line spacing, find that this
will fit on one page. Perhaps
you could work out a similar
idea to print out the directory
in 4 columns a la TABLOID and
include this on future discs.

          Kind regards,

        Peter R. Morgalla


Brian Cavers to Peter Morgalla

The TABLOID printout you sent
looks similar to the occasional
hiccup I get with my printer. It
seems it sometimes can't cope
and skips or corrupts a byte and
then everything that follows may
be out of line. TABLOID itself I
have tested extensively so I do
not think it is the program but
I've re-written a lot of TABLOID
now. Please try this new version
and report again.

I already have a 3 or 4 column
directory routine and will try
to put it in OUTLET A.S.A.P.

                         -Brian

From J. Manning, PETERBOROUGH

Dear Ron & Brian Cavers,

Thank you for the tape every
month. It does rather stretch my
mind but this is good.At 67 some
of the previously well-trodden
paths were becoming a little
overgrown. Again many thanks to
you both.

I have just acquired a Spectrum
+3 complete with an Amstrad FD-1
2nd drive. This, together with
the 120D printer I already have,
work together very well. One of
my difficulties has been getting
a print out of the Editorial and
letters from the tape but enter-
ing the two pokes 23354, 62 and

23355,16. Then FORMAT LPRINT "U"
before entering the tape. Then,
after loading selecting "T" from
the heading and then "L" from
the print options,my own Tabloid
copy was coming right off the
press. Three beautiful columns
of print. What a program!I still
cannot print the main CONTENTS
page though.

I am also not getting on too
well trying to copy from tape to
disk. I would like to request
two 3" disks from your back
issues. If you could possibly
choose them for me! A loader or
dump program or something is
possibly needed?
            Yours, many thanks,
               J. Manning

Brian Cavers to J. Manning

You can copy the CONTENTS page
to a printer using HURRYDUMP. It
is in OUTLET 9 (too early for +3
but get the tape version). I
also recommend CATLOADER (OUTLET
33) which will make using your
two +3 drives so much easier. It
gives you easier copying from
disc to disc, erasing etc. as
well as loading. I use it all
the time.
                        - Brian.

From Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Can anyone please advise ?. How can I reduce the level of interference put out by the +D and/or the Spectrum so that I can use them with a morse decode software program fed from the loudspeaker output of my short- wave receiver. When the +D 'turns', the noise it generates just blots out my short wave radio. Even my tv adds noise.

Help please someone !!!

Brian Gaff to Malcolm Goodman

This is a common problem and I am afraid there is no one answer to it. You could for instance coat the inside of all casings with conductive paint, then earth it, and screen the cables. However, as long as you have a direct connection to the receiver, the mush will get in!

Most Hams use terminal units which can have an opto-isolator in them. This breaks the direct connection, and, with good screening and an aerial as far away from the computer/TV as possible, the problem is much reduced.

For more info, I feel sure the RSGB could point you toward a Ham computing club who may have already solved your particular problem.

I have myself experienced the interference you mention, and the only thing I found that helped a bit was to wind the lead that carries the signal to the Spectrum, around a ferrite torroid a few times. This seemed to be best done at the Spectrum end. I hope that helps.

- Brian Gaff

Dear Brian & Ron,

Re. Paul Preston's enquiry in OUTLET 44 about the Opus Discovery "File Manipulation Table". This is TABLE #14 which tabulates the start addresses for DOS routines as follows:-

199F.TABLE_14...DEFB 0

19A0...DEFW 19A2

19A2...DEFW 0D18 ; MAKE_CAT opens the CAT channel. On entry DE points to the start of the parameter block, BC holds the length of the block and A holds the 'channel_open' flags.

19A4...DEFW 0BB0 ; PUT_BLK writes a block to disc.

19A6...DEFW 0D81 ; FIND_FL find a file having the same name as that stored at (IX+8). On exit the 'record_No' is in BC.

19A8...DEFW 0DE8 ; MAKE_FL make a file in the CAT.

19AA...DEFW 0DA8 ; GET_FRE find the largest gap on the disc. On exit BC holds the length of the gap and DE holds the record No. of the file preceding the gap. Note that if two gaps of the same length are found, the first is ignored.

19AC...DEFW 0E8C ; POSN_BC find the record No. held in BC from the CAT file.

19AE...DEFW 0E83 ; READ_CAT reads a byte from the CAT file into the A reg. On exit HL holds the address of the byte in the buffer.

19B0...DEFW 0ABB ; WRITE_CAT writes a byte from the A reg to disc.

The above is how the table appears in version 2.1 DOS. In version 2.2, things are shuffled about a bit, and TABLE 14 sits at 1812H and will look like this, to find similar routines at relevant addresses:-

1812 DEFB 0 1813 DEFW 1815 1815 DEFW 0DD4 ; MAKE_CAT 1817 DEFW 0C63 ; PUT_BLK 1819 DEFW 0E3D ; FIND_FL 181B DEFW 0EA4 ; MAKE_FL 181D DEFW 0E64 ; GET_FRE 181F DEFW 0F48 ; POSN_BC 1821 DEFW 0F3F ; READ_CAT 1823 DEFW 0B6E ; WRITE_CAT

What a genius! I hear you cry, to disassemble the Discovery ROM just like that. But as the applause fades away, I must confess that I extracted the info from a disassembly produced by Marcel van Dongen, which I obtained from him in 1989. His address then was, and probably still is:-

Fred Ruyschstr.65, 2563 VW Den Haag, Holland.

```text
        Tel: 070/600153.
```

...and he charged 18 Guilders (approx `6) for it. Although Marcel writes excellent English, deciphering the book is tedious as it has been photocopied with rather poor definition. So 4s can be mistaken for As, Bs for 8s, Ds for 0s, Es for Fs etc., but it does exist and the 108 pages are crammed full of useful information. The main section is a full disassembly of the 2.1 DOS, then follow 4 appendices:-

A: Routines in 2.2 and 2.22.

B: Memory map.

C: Data sheet for the W01770, plus some tables that are virtually unreadable in my copy, plus a flag summary.

D: Organisation of the disc, sectors,tracks, blocks, records.

And last of all, a good index to the routines, giving addresses for both 2.1 and 2.2 versions.

Hope this helps.   Chris Oliver.

Many thanks, Chris. - Brian

Brian Gaff to Haydn McWatters

There is no way I know of to operate a +D and Interface 1 at the same time. Both have a ROM which pages in when there is a syntax error in normal Spectrum Basic so they just fight each other for control!

The Brother HR5 does come in two variants, as you say, but as to whether it is possible to actua- lly add the other to an existing printer, I very much doubt it!

The VTX 5000 works with a +D but I doubt if the disc interface will be reliable when mounted on the ribbon cable.The cable skews the very high frequency pulses and that confuses the +D!

The grey +2 RS232 has a serial port which uses a plug very similar to the BT telephone ones. They are available from Tandy etc. Note that the RS232 software in ROM is very crude compared to Interface 1,you need 2 pokes to create a "b" channel!

The only problem is I know of no +2 that has ever successfully driven both a +D and a VTX5000 simultaneously. The reason is that the extra chips in the 128K machine lessen the peripheral driving power quite a lot.

The VTX 5000 also needs a short MC routine to boot in the ROM on a +2, though if you use software loaded from disc, this is not a problem.

There can also be a clash of roms if OPENTYPE files are in use when a VTX ROM routine is called.

If you use a 48K machine, you could connect the VTX and +D via a Currah Uslot, though the disc interface would stick up in the air.
